questions.prompt: A bank links its branch offices in Delhi, Chennai and Kolkata into one network. Which type of network is this?
questions.explanation: A network spreading across cities or countries is a WAN (Wide Area Network). A LAN covers only a building or campus.

questions.prompt: Which type of network is formed when a phone connects to wireless earbuds using Bluetooth?
questions.explanation: A PAN (Personal Area Network) covers the few metres around one person's own devices.

questions.prompt: Which device converts a computer's digital signals into signals that can travel over a telephone line, and converts them back again?
questions.explanation: A modem modulates and demodulates signals so digital data can pass over analogue lines.

questions.prompt: Which device is used to regenerate a weakening signal so it can travel farther along a cable?
questions.explanation: A repeater amplifies or regenerates the signal to extend the distance it can cover.

questions.prompt: Which topology connects all devices to one common main cable called the backbone?
questions.explanation: In a bus topology every node taps into a single shared backbone cable.

questions.prompt: In which topology is every device directly connected to every other device, giving many alternate paths?
questions.explanation: A mesh has links between all nodes, so data can take another route if one link fails, though it needs a lot of cabling.

questions.prompt: What does DNS do when you type www.example.com into a browser?

expected_answer.value: It translates the domain name into an IP address

options: It translates the domain name into an IP address
It encrypts the web page before sending it
It stores a permanent copy of the website on your computer
It assigns a new IP address to your computer
questions.explanation: DNS works like a phone book, converting a human-friendly name into the numeric IP address of the server.

questions.prompt: Why are domain names used instead of asking people to type IP addresses?

expected_answer.value: Names are easier for people to remember

options: IP addresses cannot be used on the Internet
Names are easier for people to remember
Domain names travel faster than IP addresses
Domain names do not need to be resolved
questions.explanation: Domain names are memorable; DNS maps them to the numeric addresses computers actually use.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a valid IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: IPv4 has four numbers, each from 0 to 255, separated by dots. 256 is out of range and the others have the wrong number of parts.

questions.prompt: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long. Why was IPv6 introduced?
options: IPv4 could not be used with websites
IPv6 makes every website load instantly
questions.explanation: IPv4 has only about 4.3 billion addresses; IPv6 provides a vastly larger address space.

questions.prompt: Which part of a web address shows that data between your browser and the site is encrypted?
questions.explanation: The 's' in https stands for secure; it means the connection uses encryption (TLS).

questions.prompt: A padlock icon next to a website address mainly indicates that:

expected_answer.value: the connection to the site is encrypted

options: every page on the site is free of viruses
the site is owned by the government
the connection to the site is encrypted
the site's content is always true
questions.explanation: The padlock shows the data in transit is encrypted; it does not vouch for the honesty or safety of the content.

questions.prompt: Which tag holds the visible content of a web page, such as paragraphs and images?
questions.explanation: Content shown in the browser window goes inside <body>; <head> holds information about the page.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct basic skeleton of an HTML page?
questions.explanation: The <html> element contains <head> first and then <body>; they are siblings, not nested in each other.

questions.prompt: Which code displays the word Sale in italics?
questions.explanation: <i> italicises text, <b> makes it bold, <u> underlines it and <sub> lowers it.

questions.prompt: Which code shows the 2 in the chemical formula H2O as a subscript?
questions.explanation: <sub> lowers text below the baseline; <sup> raises it.

questions.prompt: Which tag correctly inserts the image file logo.png into a page?
questions.explanation: The image tag is and the file is given in the src attribute; href is used by links.

questions.prompt: Which code creates a link with the text Visit that goes to https://example.com ?
questions.explanation: A hyperlink uses the <a> tag with the destination in href and the clickable text between the tags.

questions.prompt: Which tag creates a row in an HTML table?
questions.explanation: <tr> is a table row; <td> and <th> are cells inside it.

questions.prompt: Which code produces a bulleted list of Tea and Milk?
questions.explanation: <ul> gives an unordered (bulleted) list with <li> items; <ol> would number them.

questions.prompt: An email that pretends to be from your bank and asks you to enter your password on a fake page is an example of:
questions.explanation: Phishing tricks people into revealing private information by imitating a trusted source.

questions.prompt: Which malicious program attaches itself to files and spreads when those files are opened or shared?
questions.explanation: A virus replicates by infecting other files; a firewall and antivirus are protective tools.

questions.prompt: Which password would be hardest for an attacker to guess?
questions.explanation: A strong password is long and mixes upper and lower case letters, digits and symbols without personal details.

questions.prompt: You get a message saying you have won a prize and must click a link and enter your bank details. What is the best action?

expected_answer.value: Do not click; delete it and report it as spam

options: Click the link to check if it is genuine
Do not click; delete it and report it as spam
Reply with your account number to claim the prize
Forward it to all your friends
questions.explanation: Unexpected prize messages asking for bank details are typical scams; avoid the link and report it.

questions.prompt: Copying paragraphs from a website into your project and submitting them as your own work is:
questions.explanation: Presenting someone else's words as your own without credit is plagiarism.

questions.prompt: Copyright law protects:

expected_answer.value: the original expression of a creator's work, such as a song or a book

options: the original expression of a creator's work, such as a song or a book
any common word or colour name
only physical objects such as machines
only works that have been sold
questions.explanation: Copyright gives creators rights over their original creative works from the moment they are created.

questions.prompt: When A = 1 and B = 0, which expression has the value 1?
questions.explanation: OR is 1 if either input is 1. A AND B = 0, NOT A = 0 and (NOT A) OR B = 0 OR 0 = 0.

questions.prompt: When A = 1, B = 0 and C = 1, which expression has the value 0?
questions.explanation: AND needs both inputs to be 1, and B is 0. The other expressions all evaluate to 1.

questions.prompt: By De Morgan's law, NOT (A AND B) is equal to:
questions.explanation: De Morgan: negating an AND gives the OR of the negations.

questions.prompt: By De Morgan's law, NOT (A OR B) is equal to:
questions.explanation: Negating an OR gives the AND of the negations.

questions.prompt: Cells B2 to B5 contain 10, 20, 30 and 40. What does =SUM(B2:B5) give?
questions.explanation: SUM adds all values in the range: 10 + 20 + 30 + 40 = 100.

questions.prompt: Which formula finds the largest value in cells C1 to C10?
questions.explanation: MAX returns the largest number in a range; MIN gives the smallest, and COUNT only counts numeric cells.

questions.prompt: Cell C2 contains =A2*$B$1. If this formula is copied to C3, what will C3 contain?
questions.explanation: The relative reference A2 moves down to A3, while the absolute reference $B$1 stays fixed.

questions.prompt: Which cell reference does not change when the formula is copied to any other cell?
questions.explanation: Dollar signs before both column and row make the reference fully absolute.

questions.prompt: Besides the main document, what does a mail merge need?

expected_answer.value: A data source with the recipients' details

options: A data source with the recipients' details
An empty spreadsheet with no names
questions.explanation: Mail merge combines a main letter with a data source such as a table of names and addresses.

questions.prompt: In a mail merge, a placeholder like «Name» in the main document is called a:
questions.explanation: Merge fields are replaced with data from each record of the data source.

questions.prompt: Which of the following correctly defines an algorithm?

expected_answer.value: a finite, step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem

options: a finite, step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a clear sequence of steps leading to a solution; it is independent of any particular language.

questions.prompt: Which is an essential property of a good algorithm?

expected_answer.value: It must end after a finite number of steps

options: It must be written in Python
It must have at least ten steps
It must always contain a loop
It must end after a finite number of steps
questions.explanation: An algorithm must terminate; it need not use any language, specific length or loop.

questions.prompt: Which flowchart symbol is used for a decision with Yes/No branches?
questions.explanation: A diamond represents a condition being tested, with branches for each outcome.

questions.prompt: Which flowchart symbol is used for input and output?
questions.explanation: The parallelogram marks input or output steps such as reading a number or printing a result.

questions.prompt: Breaking a large problem into smaller, manageable sub-problems is called:
questions.explanation: Decomposition splits a complex task into parts that are easier to solve.

questions.prompt: You want to display the numbers 1 to 100 without writing 100 separate statements. What should you use?
questions.explanation: A loop repeats a set of instructions, so one block can handle all 100 numbers.

questions.prompt: Saving a PDF from your school's website onto your laptop is an example of:
questions.explanation: Downloading copies a file from a remote computer to your own device.

questions.prompt: A computer that stores web pages and sends them when a browser asks is called a:
questions.explanation: A web server holds website files and responds to browser requests.

questions.prompt: Which protocol is used to send an email from your computer to the mail server?
questions.explanation: SMTP sends mail out; POP3 retrieves it from the server.

questions.prompt: Which protocol is used to download your incoming email from a mail server to your computer?
questions.explanation: POP3 fetches stored messages from the mailbox; SMTP is for sending.

questions.prompt: Which tool transfers files over an encrypted connection?
questions.explanation: SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) encrypts the data; plain FTP sends it unprotected.

questions.prompt: Why is TELNET considered unsafe for remote login?

expected_answer.value: It sends data, including passwords, as plain text

options: It sends data, including passwords, as plain text
It cannot log in to remote computers
It needs a paid licence for every login
It only works inside one building
questions.explanation: TELNET does not encrypt traffic, so passwords can be read by anyone intercepting it; SSH is the secure alternative.

questions.prompt: Transferring money using your bank's mobile app is an example of:
questions.explanation: e-Banking means carrying out banking transactions over the Internet.

questions.prompt: Which Internet service lets people in different cities see and hear each other live during a meeting?
questions.explanation: Video conferencing transmits live audio and video between participants.

questions.prompt: Which service can carry pictures, audio and video clips in a message, unlike plain text-only messages?
questions.explanation: MMS (Multimedia Messaging Service) supports multimedia; SMS is limited to short text.

questions.prompt: Which of these is the latest and fastest generation of mobile network?
questions.explanation: Each generation improved speed; 5G is the most recent of those listed.

questions.prompt: Which code sets the background colour of the page to yellow?
questions.explanation: bgcolor sets the background colour of the body; text sets the colour of the text.

questions.prompt: The text placed inside which tag appears on the browser's title bar or tab?
questions.explanation: <title>, placed inside <head>, gives the page name shown on the tab.

questions.prompt: Which tag starts a new line without starting a new paragraph?
questions.explanation:
is a line break;
draws a horizontal rule and

starts a paragraph.

questions.prompt: Which heading tag gives the largest heading text by default?
questions.explanation: Headings run from <h1> (largest) to <h6> (smallest); <head> is not a heading.

questions.prompt:
Look at this code:
  1. Red
  2. Blue
. How is the second item labelled?
questions.explanation: type="A" makes the list use capital letters, so items are A, B, C and so on.

questions.prompt: What numbers will the three items show in <ol start="5"> with three <li> items?
questions.explanation: start sets the first number, and the rest continue from it.

questions.prompt: Which attribute of gives the text shown if the image cannot be displayed?
questions.explanation: alt supplies alternative text for missing images and screen readers.

questions.prompt: Which code adds an audio player with play and pause buttons for song.mp3?
questions.explanation: The <audio> tag takes the file in src, and the controls attribute shows the player buttons.

questions.prompt: Which attribute makes a table cell stretch across two columns?
questions.explanation: colspan spans columns; rowspan spans rows.

questions.prompt: Which tag defines a heading cell in a table, shown bold and centred by default?
questions.explanation: <th> is a table header cell, while <td> is an ordinary data cell.

questions.prompt: A form asks pupils to select exactly one house: Red, Blue, Green or Yellow. Which control suits this best?
questions.explanation: Radio buttons in one group allow only one choice; checkboxes allow several.

questions.prompt: Which input type hides the characters typed, showing dots instead?
questions.explanation: A password field masks what is typed.

questions.prompt: Which link opens the user's email program with a message addressed to help@school.in ?
questions.explanation: The mailto: scheme in href starts a new email to that address.

questions.prompt: Which attribute makes a link open in a new browser tab?
questions.explanation: target="_blank" opens the destination in a new tab or window; _self uses the same one.

questions.prompt: Which CSS rule makes all paragraph text red?
questions.explanation: The text colour property in CSS is color, written as property: value.

questions.prompt: Which CSS property sets the space outside an element's border?
questions.explanation: Margin is the space outside the border; padding is the space inside it.

questions.prompt: Typing a whole message in capital letters online is generally seen as:
questions.explanation: Capitals are read as raising your voice, so good netiquette avoids it.

questions.prompt: Before posting a photograph of a classmate online, what should you do?
options: Post it at once and tell them later
Tag everyone in the class without asking
Edit it so it looks funny
questions.explanation: Respecting others' privacy means getting consent before sharing their pictures.

questions.prompt: Software whose source code is freely available for anyone to study and modify is called:
questions.explanation: Open-source licences allow users to view, change and share the source code.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an open-source operating system?
questions.explanation: Linux is open-source; Windows and macOS are proprietary, and Photoshop is an application, not an operating system.

questions.prompt: Which action helps you avoid plagiarism when using ideas from an article?

expected_answer.value: Quote or paraphrase it and credit the author

options: Copy it and leave out the author's name
Change a few words and give no credit
Use it without reading it fully
Quote or paraphrase it and credit the author
questions.explanation: Giving credit to the source for quoted or paraphrased material is the way to avoid plagiarism.

questions.prompt: IPR stands for:
questions.explanation: IPR are legal rights over creations of the mind, such as writings, inventions and designs.

questions.prompt: Before typing your card details on a shopping site, what should you check?

expected_answer.value: The address starts with https and a padlock is shown

options: That the site has many advertisements
That it offers the highest discounts
That it asks for your PIN by email
The address starts with https and a padlock is shown
questions.explanation: https and the padlock show an encrypted connection; genuine sites never ask for a PIN by email.

questions.prompt: Which of these should you never share with anyone, even someone claiming to be from the bank?

expected_answer.value: The OTP received on your phone

options: The OTP received on your phone
questions.explanation: An OTP authorises a transaction; sharing it lets others take money from your account.
